title: rwb-access access-review extract (JOB-18): the interface ID, the file pattern, the extract layout, the recipient and the review-cycle date convention are not specified, the two requester activity names and the manifest are named by no source, and the delivery events are keyed by case ID while an access-review file has no case
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14, 16, 41, 43 and 44 (slide 44 JOB-18 Access review list, six-monthly, rwb-access, Schedule; slide 14 P4 contract; slide 16 P2 outbound-file contract); Legacy RWB-E1-007 sections 3, 4, 12 and 16; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A1.2 and A2.3-A2.7; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 and T3.2; RWB-P2-E1007-CON sections 12.3 and 12.5; Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 section R5.5 DP-16 and section R9
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5; section 11 Data; section 12.2, 12.4, 12.5 and 12.8; section 13 Configuration and reference data; section 14 Validation and messages; section 15 Screens and states
description: Six values a requester-side slice of the outbound-file capability needs are absent from every source. (1) The access-review file has no interface ID: Architecture v5 slide 44 gives the job only as 'Access review list, six-monthly, rwb-access, Schedule', and no extract names INT-14, INT-19, INT-20, INT-25 or any other row as the access-review interface. (2) Its file name pattern, its data product and its alert role are therefore absent too, although this story takes them from the interface row rather than from code. (3) The extract layout, the columns it carries and the record it counts are not described anywhere: FSD P4 v3 A1.2 lists 31 features and none is the review extract, TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines the four tables and no extract, and the legacy story RWB-E1-007 describes the WIN, INT-19, INT-20 and INT-25 files but no access-review file. (4) The recipient of the file and the body that receives it are unnamed. (5) The review-cycle date convention is unnamed: no source says whether the six-monthly run's business date is the effective date of the cycle, the first or the last day of the period, or the period covered. (6) The delivery contract of RWB-P2-E1007-CON keys `FileDelivered` and `FileFailed` by case ID, and an access-review file carries no case, so the key of a file-level delivery and the way a requesting service without cases matches an outcome to its request are not stated. Two further shapes this story had to fix are carried by the assumption rows rather than described as source values: the names, inputs and outputs of `buildAccessReviewFile` and `requestFileDelivery`, and the manifest element list of a requesting service. Nothing here blocks a build, because every value is a row, a parameter or a manifest element read at run time, and no literal appears in code.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 reads 'JOB-18 | Access review list | six-monthly | rwb-access | Schedule' with no interface, no layout and no recipient; slide 14 reads 'TMP Schedule: access review list (six-monthly)' and names no file; slide 16 gives P2 'deliverFile(manifest)' and the two events but no access-review interface; slide 11 fixes the claim-check manifest as 'fileId, batchId, sha256, record count' only; slide 43 reads 'FileDelivered, FileFailed | rwb-integration | rwb.integration.events.v1 | requesting service'. RWB-P2-E1007-CON 12.3 names the key of both events as caseId and its payload carries interfaceId and businessDate. FSD P4 v3 A1.2 enumerates FEAT-ACA-01 to FEAT-ACA-16 and FEAT-ADM-01 to FEAT-ADM-14 with no review-extract feature; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines role, permission, delegation_limit, lov_value, masking_rule, role_conflict, partner_user, rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case, and no extract or staging object. Legacy RWB-E1-007 section 12 lists JOB-10, JOB-11, JOB-13 and JOB-15 with their inputs and outputs; no JOB-18 row, no access-review interface and no review layout appears in it or in its section 16. No source read names a review file pattern, a recipient or a cycle-date rule, and no source states how a requesting service with no case matches a delivery outcome.
area: rwb-access access-review extract, its interface row and the key of the file-level delivery events
owner_role: Solution architect, P4 with the rwb-integration contract owner
proposed: At the RWB-P2-E1007-CON review, register one interface row for the access-review file in the interface configuration version in force with its interface ID, direction OUTBOUND, file pattern, data product, owner role and alert role, and publish the extract layout and the recipient with RWB-P4-AD008-APP. Agree with the rwb-integration contract owner how a file-level delivery with no case is matched, by interfaceId and businessDate rather than by the case key, and state the review-cycle date convention in RWB-P4-AD008-APP. Nothing here blocks the build: this story reads every value at run time and writes the placeholder wherever a literal would appear.

title: The case-authority request shape, the source of the caller teams and regions, and the case-record personal field list are not fixed by any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1, T6.2 and T-A.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4, A2.5, A2.11, A2.14 and A2.30; Legacy RWB-E1-018 sections 3, 4, 10, 11 and 14
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 1 to 8; section 7 AC1 to AC8; section 11 Data; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Configuration
description: Architecture v5 names POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise (role, scope, DoA) and GET /me/permissions as the first API paths of rwb-access and calls the answer cached, but neither Architecture v5 nor TSD P4 appendix T-A gives the request or the answer schema of the authorise path, and T-A.2 defines only API-P4-012 GET /me/session. The case-authority slice therefore has to fix, as a default, which case facts travel in the request (case reference, owner, queue, team, region) and what the answer carries (decision code, right, scope applied, matrix version, masking version, marker per field ID). Second, no source holds where the caller's own teams and regions live: TSD P4 T3.1 defines role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit only, queue and queue_member are rwb-case's under the ownership rulings, and LOV-SCOPE names OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL without saying what TEAM and REGION are matched against. Third, the roster of personal field IDs of the case record that this service must answer markers for is not listed anywhere; FSD P4 A2.7 names DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 as masked on the case record view and FSD P4 A2.5 names the masking version MASK-SIT-01 without listing the fields it covers.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 lists rwb-access IN as REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies with no schema; slide 41 gives /authorise as the first API path of the service; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is the authorise path, and T-A.2 API-P4-012 defines GET /me/session only; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 defines six tables and none holds a user, team or region membership; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE lists OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL; FSD P4 v3 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 names DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 marked masked; FSD P4 v3 A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 names masking version MASK-SIT-01 with no rule for v_ace_customer.date_of_birth; Legacy RWB-E1-018 section 10 gives the role list and section 14 the two messages, and neither gives a request or answer shape.
proposed: Add the case-authority request and answer schema to the API specification and TSD P4 appendix T-A, publish it with RWB-P4-E1037-CON so rwb-case and the screens build against one shape, record in TSD P4 T3.1 where the caller's teams and regions are held (or confirm that they travel with the session resolved at sign-in), and list the case-record personal field IDs the masking pack must cover with their version, so the story's three defaults become source values.

title: rwb-access policy and catalogue answers: no source names the request and answer field set of the role catalogue, the masking policy read or the data-product authorise answer, nor the marker vocabulary or the masking-exceptions part
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-access IN: POST /authorise, GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits, /masking-policies) and slide 41 (P4 owns Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles, Response Role[]) and T3.1 (role, permission, masking_rule); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.3, A2.4, A2.5 and A2.30; Ownership Map (data_product, data_product_access, sys_fields, sys_objects owned by P1); Legacy RWB-E1-016 sections 7, 11 and 12
section: Section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 4 and 9; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC1, AC3 and AC4; section 12.1 Contract; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 15 Screens and states
description: Three answers of this slice have no field set in any source. API-P4-007 gives GET /admin/roles the response name Role[] and the purpose 'list roles with permissions and scope' but no field list, no version field and no masking part; TSD P4 T3.1 defines the columns of role and permission, from which a field set can be inferred, but not the shape of the answer or whether one role entry embeds its permission rows. Architecture v5 slide 14 names /masking-policies and POST /authorise without a request or answer schema, and neither operation appears in TSD P4 appendix T-A. The marker vocabulary is not fixed either: the FSD describes a masked rendering (XXXX-XX-XX, XXXXXX5678) while this service must answer a marker and never a rendering. The role catalogue is required to carry masking exceptions, and no source says that the catalogue carries them at all or what an exception is. The story therefore fixes the field set, the marker values masked and clear, the maskingExceptions part and the access resolution the authorise request carries, and the contract review has to confirm or rename them before the endpoints are frozen.
evidence: TSD P4 T-A.2 API-P4-007: Response 'Role[]', no schema; no entry for /masking-policies or /authorise in T-A.1; Architecture v5 slide 14 lists the two paths with no payload; TSD P4 T3.1 gives columns only, with matrix_version on permission and masking_version on masking_rule but no version field on the answer; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 and AC-ALT-P4-004-01 describe masked renderings (XXXX-XX-XX, XXXXXXXXX1234) and no marker; no source describes a masking exception as a field ID whose row says unmasked true.
proposed: Publish the request and answer schemas of GET /admin/roles, GET /masking-policies and POST /authorise in TSD P4 appendix T-A and in the OpenAPI file of the service, with the marker values, the maskingExceptions part, the two version fields and the access resolution the request carries, so the contract is frozen once and not inferred per story.

title: rwb-access local decision-record store: the column set behind the five named columns, the canonical form, the genesis value, the verifier behaviour on write and read, the DECISION_LOG letters per role and the per-service login are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 20, 28, 41, 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 (decision record fields, JOB-14); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.7, A2.8 and A2.26; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T3.2 (LOV-CAPABILITY), T6.1, T6.2 and API-P4-008; Legacy RWB-E1-008 sections 4 to 13
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 4, 11, 12 and 13; section 8 Business rules BR4, BR6, BR9 and BR10; section 12.1 and 12.7 Contract; section 13 Solution plan
description: Six values this slice needs are absent or unresolved. (1) The Work Package names five columns of the local table - chain_seq, prev_hash, entry_hash, corrects_entry_id and actor_user_id - and Architecture v5 slide 20 names the table decision_record, but no source publishes its full column set or physical types, so the entry fields are taken from DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 and the rest is a design choice. (2) The canonical form and the SHA-256 hashing rule are fixed by the legacy story for the monolith table, not for the per-service library object, and the library contract does not carry them. (3) The genesis value, the advisory-lock key of the per-service chain and the trigger name in each service schema are unnamed. (4) No source states what the verifier does on a write and on a read of the local chain: the legacy story describes the daily range check only, and the 02:00 Schedule, its 15-minute report and the daily seal stay with rwb-decision (JOB-14). (5) The letters each role holds in the DECISION_LOG capability area are not tabulated: TSD P4 T6.1 has columns for Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration only, while T3.2 lists DECISION_LOG among the 14 areas, and TSD P4 API-P4-008 names Platform administration R for the /admin/access-log path. (6) The per-service database login name of rwb-access is named nowhere.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 20 gives every service 'Own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record' and slide 28 describes the local record, hash-linked, without a column list; slide 44 gives JOB-14 to rwb-decision at 02:00; Temporal design slide 16 lists chain_seq, inputsRef, ruleId, ruleVersion, recommendation, approverUserId, approvalLevel, finalCall, actions, outcome, decidedAt, prev_hash and entry_hash for the record and adds 'JOB-14 checks the chain at 02:00'; TSD P4 T6.1 tabulates three capability columns only, T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY lists DECISION_LOG, and T-A.1 API-P4-008 declares 'Platform administration, right R' for GET /admin/access-log; legacy RWB-E1-008 BR4 fixes the canonical form for the monolith table and section 13 names property rwb.decision.chain.genesis-hash without a value for a per-service chain.
area: rwb-access local decision-record store, chain verification and Decision log right
proposed: Publish the decision_record column set, its physical types and the canonical-form rule once in the shared library specification (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) and let every service schema take them from there; add the DECISION_LOG column to the TSD P4 RBAC matrix and confirm whether the local read keeps Platform administration R as well; fix the per-service login names in the platform DB story; state in the Temporal and Drools design what the local verifier does on a write and on a read, so the daily JOB-14 check is the only Scheduled check.

title: Role version: roster, row counts, role-file layout, matrix effective date, conflict list and MSG-P4-006 text not specified
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 (T3.1, T3.2, T6.1); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 (A2.3, A2.4); legacy RWB-E1-019
section: TSD P4 T3.1 (role, permission, role_conflict); TSD P4 T3.2 (LOV-ROLE-CLASS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-SCOPE); TSD P4 T6.1; FSD P4 A2.3 and A2.4
description: No source states how many roles a role version holds, the layout of the approved role file, the conflict version label, the column that dates a matrix version, or the full list of conflicting role pairs. TSD P4 T3.1 gives role and permission no valid_from and no valid_to, while FSD P4 A2.4 takes matrix file PM-2026.12 into effect on 2026-12-01, so the target has no named column to date a matrix version. The only conflict pairs a source names are RW-SECADM with any business role (FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-03) and RW-RISK not holding RW-REFADM (legacy RWB-E1-019 section 10), and no source gives the text of MSG-P4-006.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.1 role (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039) and permission (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044) carry no valid_from and no valid_to; role_conflict (DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211) carries conflict_version, valid_from and valid_to with no value in any source; TSD P4 T6.1 lists the role codes column by capability with no count and no roster file; FSD P4 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01 names matrix versions PM-2026.11 and PM-2026.12 with 756 permission rows and validFrom 2026-12-01; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-02 uses a duplicate role and area row and the letters RX as refused examples; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 refuses a session holding RW-SECADM and RW-CASEOWN with MSG-P4-006 and gives no text; legacy RWB-E1-019 section 10 states RW-RISK may not hold RW-REFADM.
area: rwb-access role catalogue, permission matrix and role conflict data
owner_role: Security administrator (RW-SECADM), with the reference data administrator (RW-REFADM)
proposed: Confirm with the security administrator, before the role version is frozen, the layout of the approved role file, the role and permission row counts of the version in force, the conflict version label, the column that holds the effective date of a matrix version, the full conflict list and the text of MSG-P4-006; until then the story seeds exactly the rows of the approved file and cites this row wherever a value is missing.
